abstracts.abstract: The increasing complexity of modern web applications demands a fundamental shift in how we conceptualize web architecture evolution. This paper presents a unified theoretical framework for understanding and predicting web application evolution patterns, termed the Web Architecture Dynamics Theory (WADT). Unlike existing approaches that treat web evolution as an ad-hoc process, WADT formalizes web application components as dynamic graph structures, where nodes represent functional modules and edges capture dependency relationships. We introduce novel metrics based on information theory and complex network analysis to quantify architectural entropy, coupling intensity, and cohesion degradation over time. The framework establishes formal relationships between code change patterns, architectural smells accumulation, and system quality attributes such as maintainability and performance. Through rigorous mathematical derivations, we prove that web applications follow predictable evolution trajectories characterized by distinct phases: stable growth, technical debt accumulation, and critical transition points. Empirical validation on 150 open-source web systems spanning multiple technology stacks demonstrates that WADT predicts architectural decay patterns with 87% accuracy, enabling proactive refactoring decisions. This paradigm-shifting framework provides web engineers with a scientific foundation for making architectural decisions that account for long-term system evolution, fundamentally transforming how we approach web engineering practices.

Traditional threat modeling methodologies developed for monolithic web applications prove inadequate when applied to contemporary microservice-based architectures. This paper presents an enhanced threat modeling framework that systematically extends the STRIDE methodology to address the unique security challenges of modern web services. We identify critical gaps in existing approaches, including the neglect of inter-service trust boundaries, API attack surfaces, and data flow complexities introduced by service mesh architectures. Our enhanced framework introduces three novel dimensions: Service Dependency Threat Analysis (SDTA), API Contract Vulnerability Assessment, and Distributed Transaction Security Modeling. We formalize threat propagation patterns through petri nets, enabling the identification of cascading security failures across service boundaries. The framework incorporates a weighted threat scoring mechanism that considers both technical severity and business impact, providing prioritized remediation guidance. Evaluation across twelve enterprise-scale microservice applications reveals that our approach identifies 43% more security threats than conventional methods, with particularly significant improvements in identifying API-level vulnerabilities and inter-service authentication weaknesses. The proposed framework maintains backward compatibility with existing security processes while providing substantially enhanced coverage for complex web service ecosystems.

Component reuse across different web frameworks remains a fundamental challenge in modern web development, despite advances in component-based architectures. This paper introduces AutoWeaver, a revolutionary declarative web application composition system that fundamentally transforms how developers create web applications by enabling true cross-framework component interoperability. AutoWeaver introduces the Component Intent Specification (CIS), a novel abstraction that allows developers to declare component functionality, behavior, and presentation semantics independently of any specific framework. The system employs a sophisticated semantic translation engine that automatically transforms CIS specifications into optimized implementations for target frameworks including React, Vue, Angular, and Svelte. The architecture includes a semantic equivalence verification layer ensuring behavioral consistency across all generated implementations. We present a comprehensive formal specification of the CIS language, including its type system, composition operators, and transformation rules. Implementation of the AutoWeaver compiler achieves a translation speed of approximately 50 components per second while maintaining full semantic fidelity. Evaluation across a benchmark suite of 200 components demonstrates that AutoWeaver achieves 94% behavioral equivalence compared to manually developed framework-specific implementations, while reducing development time by an average of 67%. This paradigm-shifting approach establishes a new direction for web engineering that transcends framework boundaries.

Progressive Web Applications introduce unique performance characteristics that conventional testing frameworks fail to adequately address, including service worker behavior, cache management strategies, and offline functionality validation. This paper presents AdaptTest, an adaptive performance testing framework specifically designed for PWA testing that dynamically optimizes test strategies based on application characteristics. The framework implements a three-phase approach: intelligent feature detection that automatically identifies PWA-specific components, adaptive test case generation that creates targeted scenarios based on detected features, and real-time performance anomaly detection using statistical process control methods. We introduce the PWA Performance Quality Index (PPQI), a composite metric that captures loading performance, runtime efficiency, and offline capability across various network conditions. The system architecture incorporates a lightweight instrumentation layer that monitors service worker lifecycle events, cache hit ratios, and background synchronization operations without introducing significant overhead. Evaluation across a diverse corpus of 35 production PWAs demonstrates that AdaptTest achieves 31% higher defect detection rates compared to existing tools while reducing test execution time by 45%. The framework successfully identifies performance regressions related to service worker updates, cache invalidation strategies, and network transition handling that existing methodologies overlook.
